title: Time in Store and the Step Taken in the Daily Storage Rate
content:
Grain that has stood a long while in one of the cooperative's houses is charged at a stepped-up daily rate under Grain Storage and Conditioning Agreements. Two day counts decide the step: the escalation point the programme posts, and the mid-term count of 120 days that runs across the catalogue.

## The rule as posted

Where the grain has stood in store past the programme's escalation point, the posted daily rate is the programme's daily rate stepped up by the programme's escalation percentage.

Where it has stood in store past the mid-term day count of 120 calendar days but not past the escalation point, the posted daily rate is the programme's daily rate stepped up by the mid-term percentage of 12.0 percent.

And where neither day count has been passed, the posted daily rate is the daily rate the programme posts, as it stands.

Days in store are counted in whole calendar days from the storage start date through the day the charge is worked out.

## The escalation point and step by programme

| Programme | Escalation point (calendar days) | Escalation step-up (percent) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Open Storage Account | 180 | 25.0 |
| Grain Bank Deposit Account | 240 | 20.0 |
| Commercial Warehouse Receipt Storage | 270 | 15.0 |
| Seasonal Paid-Up Storage Agreement | 365 | 30.0 |
| Conditioned Reserve Storage Agreement | 365 | 10.0 |
| Identity Preserved Segregated Storage | 365 | 10.0 |

## Both sides of each day count

Both counts are read as strictly past: a lot that has stood exactly 120 days has not stood past the mid-term count, and a lot that has stood exactly as many days as the programme's escalation point has not stood past that point. One day more, and it has.

| Days in store | Which step is taken |
| --- | --- |
| more than the programme's escalation point | the programme's escalation percentage |
| more than 120 but not more than the programme's escalation point | 12.0 percent |
| 120 or fewer | none; the posted daily rate is the programme's daily rate as it stands |

## Worked figures, on a hypothetical rate

Take an agreement whose programme posts a daily rate of 0.00200 for each bushel for each day and sets the escalation point at 180 days with a step-up of 25.0 percent.

**Days in store of 96.** Neither count has been passed, so the posted daily rate is the programme's daily rate as it stands, 0.00200.

**Days in store of 121.** The mid-term count of 120 has been passed and the escalation point has not, so the posted daily rate is the programme's daily rate stepped up by 12.0 percent, which is 0.00224.

**Days in store of 181.** The escalation point has been passed, so the posted daily rate is the programme's daily rate stepped up by that programme's 25.0 percent, which is 0.00250.
